key_insight: Data-center workload flexibility becomes usable electrical flexibility only when scheduling respects converter and network limits.
engineering_relevance: Coordinating computing workloads with on-site solar, storage, and grid purchases can reduce grid dependence without violating electrical operating limits.
method: Model synchronous training tasks with mixed-integer constraints and aggregate inference flexibility using Minkowski sums and Shapley–Folkman convexification.
Represent converter and network limits with a four-node electrical model and second-order cone relaxation.
Jointly schedule workloads, photovoltaic generation, storage, and grid purchases.
evidence_signal: Case studies found that fixed training could not support full inference service within voltage limits, while coordinated scheduling achieved negligible inference shortage and passed checks against the original AC model.
watch_item: The inference relaxation-gap bound is conditional, and results from the studied four-node system require validation before deployment in larger facilities.
paper_title: Converter-Aware Coordination of Computing Flexibility in Behind-the-Meter Data Centers
